newsitem.title: UK: Metals Outlook - Copper stocks, spreads in spotlight.
newsitem.headline: Metals Outlook - Copper stocks, spreads in spotlight.

text.p: Copper stocks and spreads will likely hold the attention of metals markets again this week, while Wednesday's option declaration is failing to generate much excitement.
Players will be sifting clues for copper's direction after nearby tightness evaporated last week and the backwardation crumbled.

The benchmark cash/threes spread was trading at a $210 backwardation early last week, but caught players by surprise by whipping in violently. Traders said the major long and the big short probably came to agreement in an off-market match-off. By Friday's close, it had narrowed to around a $70 backwardation.
Since the steam went out of the cash/May spread last week, attention has shifted to the May date and further forward.
Copper stocks rose on the last three days of last week, the first increases since February, as the backwardation sucked metal into warehouses.
Stocks ended the week 2,725 tonnes higher at 147,925 tonnes.
The deliveries into warehouses may have run their course now that tightness has eased and stocks may begin to show falls this week, analysts said.
The direction of inventories is the key to whether three months copper is able to remount a challenge to $2,400 per tonne, they added.
Last week the market peaked at $2,407 and later hit a floor at $2,325, ending the week near the middle of the range at $2,360.

A close eye will be kept on fundamental developments, especially in Chile where a band of workers called off a strike at the huge Escondida mine on Friday and a full-scale stoppage has paralysed activity at the smaller Quebrada Blanca site.
In aluminium, stocks have continued to erode, dipping below 800,000 tonnes last week. They ended the week down 11,975 tonnes at 795,250 tonnes.
Three month prices charged up to a high of $1,647 last week, but failed to sustain the move, touching a low of $1,616 on Friday and finishing the week at $1,624.

Technical indicators were looking a little more positive, after the 10-day moving average crossed above the 30-day average and prices were well above both short-term averages as well as the 100-day average, chartists said.
Wednesday's options declaration was not expected to spark much movement in the underlying contracts since there were no big lumps of open interest at relevant strikes, option dealers said.

In copper, $2,500 calls has open interest of 1,233 lots, but this was still well out of the money by the end of business on Friday, LME data showed. In aluminium, $1,650 calls show 1,309 lots of open interest, but again, this was above where the May contract ended the week.
Zinc showed moderate levels of open interest, with 450 lots at $1,250 calls and 550 lots at $1,225 puts.
